description: A green weight in the shallows, in no hurry to move, and the first thing a great many new stars ever meet.
lore: Animals fall too. The sky drops them at the same rate it drops people and sorts neither, and where a new star gets met and told what has happened to it, a frog does not, because there is nothing useful anyone can say to a frog. This one came down in the wet and carried on with the only trade it had. Sit where the flies come. Hold still. Be cold. Be patient past the point where patience is a virtue and out the far side of it, where patience is simply what a thing is made of.

That is very nearly all there is to a frog, which is what makes it so hard to say how far down this one has got. When a person loses their particulars it shows. A frog that has lost every one of its own sits in the shallows in exactly the attitude it always sat in. It has not needed to eat for longer than most of the roads have been where they are, and it still waits where the flies would come. Under it in the silt is a smooth grey-blue stone, worn round by more water than it has sat in since, cold in the palm however long the day has been — and every round wet thing out in the ponds keeps one as well.

The low end of the meadows is where people walk when they have just come down and cannot yet say their own name, so this is very often the first thing anybody meets here: a green weight the size of two hands with a hard yellow eye on each side of its head, looking back and not getting up. Going out to meet a star is the oldest courtesy in this world. The frog is not keeping it; the frog was only already there, which for a great many arrivals has had to be near enough. It is also, very often, the first thing anybody breaks — it is close, it is slow, it does not run — and afterwards somebody is standing shin-deep in cold water with a small warm stone in their hand, mottled the green of the water round their shins and already quietly at work on their knuckles. Sitting in the wet and coming out of the sitting in slightly better repair than it went in was the whole of what the animal could do. Most people begin exactly this way. The first kindness this country does them, they take off a thing that was only sitting there.
